fields.name: 代（age range・decade）
fields.meaning: Suffix 代: age range, decade (20代, 1980年代)
examples: My mother is in her forties.
This song was popular in the 1980s.
I want to go to lots of different countries while I'm in my twenties.

fields.meaning: Prefix 真っ: completely, pure (真っ赤, 真っ白)
fields.connection: 真っ + [adjective stem] (真っ赤・真っ白・真っ暗)
examples: She was so embarrassed that her face turned bright red.
It's pitch dark outside, and I can't see anything.
Pure white snow is falling.

fields.meaning: Can be seen…, is observed… (report style)
examples: New ways of using words can be seen among young people.
Many old buildings can be seen in this region.
Recently, large changes in temperature have been observed.

fields.meaning: Not a few…, quite a lot (double negative)
examples: There are quite a few students who don't eat breakfast.
There are quite a few people who travel alone.
There are also quite a few people who oppose this opinion.

fields.meaning: Suffix 化: -ization, becoming… (悪化する, 少子化)
examples: In Japan, the declining birthrate is progressing.
My illness got worse, and I was hospitalized.
The procedures have been digitized.

fields.meaning: Prefix 各: each, every… (各国, 各自)
examples: Representatives of each country gathered at the conference.
Please take your trash home with you, everyone.
Please choose two people from each class.

fields.meaning: Suffix 風: style, -style… (和風)
examples: This restaurant is famous for its Japanese-style dishes.
I feel more relaxed in a Japanese-style room than in a Western-style room.
He has an old-fashioned way of thinking.

fields.meaning: Expresses how large or small a quantity is
examples: Please form groups of four people or fewer if possible.
Packs of 500 grams or less are 50 yen off.
If you were to buy a souvenir for 3,000 yen or less, what kinds of things are there?
fields.explain: Expresses numbers below a given number, including that number itself.

fields.meaning: Can (…), be able to (…)
examples: Can you speak Arabic?
I hear that person can swim 20 or even 30 km if they go slowly.
We regret that we are unable to meet your request.
We could also reconsider "education" from the perspective of "reproducing" the members of that society or class.
fields.explain: Expresses whether there is "ability" (1. 2.) or "possibility" (3. 4.). It can be replaced with the potential form 「Ｖ－れる」, as in 「話せる」「泳げる」, but in formal situations and stiff written texts (especially when expressing possibility), 「ことができる」 tends to be somewhat preferred.

fields.meaning: That kind of …, … like that
Expresses addition
fields.connection: N/plain form + だけでなく ～ も
examples: You have to eat not only meat but also vegetables.
They're good not only at English but also at Arabic.
He not only sings well but also writes his own songs.
In the recent typhoon, the village suffered heavy damage not only to its fields but also to its houses.
He was not only invited to the award ceremony but was also asked to give a speech.
fields.explain: Means "both" or "either one." In spoken language, 「…だけじゃなく…も」 is also used.

fields.meaning: Whether … or …; … is fine, … is fine too
Expresses completion; achievement
examples: Summer vacation has finally come to an end.
My grandfather, who had been in the hospital for a long time, finally passed away.
The graduation ceremony went smoothly, and at last the day came for me to return to my country.
After 20 years, the research was finally completed.
The other person was so persistent that even he, normally so mild-mannered, finally lost his temper.
It had been cloudy since morning, and by evening it finally started to rain.
fields.explain: Expresses that something finally comes about after a long time or in the end. 1. ～3. are cases where, after a long time or process, the expected final stage is reached, and 4. is a case where the result is reached through long effort. The speaker's deep feelings about the events and years leading up to it are conveyed. Also, as in 5. 6., it is sometimes used when a state that had been maintained until then goes beyond its limit. 5. means 「ふだん怒らない彼も我慢しきれなくなって怒った」, and 6. means 「朝から雨が降りそうな天気だったが、なんとか昼の間は降らずにもっていたが、夕方には降り始めた」. Similar expressions are 「やっと」 and 「ついに」. For details, see【やっと】１.

fields.meaning: Is thought to be …, people believe that … (often when that idea is actually incorrect / needs correction)
examples: English is generally thought to be the world's common language, but in reality there are plenty of countries where English doesn't get you understood.
It had been thought that there was no life on Mars, but traces of life were confirmed in this exploration.
fields.explain: Used to state a generally accepted idea. It is often used when saying that the idea is actually incorrect or needs to be corrected.

fields.meaning: There is no … that does not … / There isn't a single … that doesn't … (double negative — every person/thing …)
… is one of the …
First of all, first (the first thing to mention)
examples: First of all, let me inform you of today's schedule.
≪Remarks by the moderator≫ Next, I would like to hear everyone's opinions. Well then, let's start with Mr. Kawaguchi.
I hear it's going to be hot this summer, so when I get my bonus, the first thing I plan to buy is an air conditioner.
As annual events in Japan, Obon and New Year's come to mind first.
To understand a country's culture, you first have to start with its language.
fields.explain: Expresses the meaning of 「最初に」「第一に」. 4. 5. mean 「他のものはさておき」.

fields.meaning: Expresses repetition or habit
examples: Apparently another plane has crashed.
I got the same question wrong again.
≪At the end of class≫ Well then, see you next week.

A: Excuse me. I'd like to take next Friday off, if I may.
B: Again? You took a day off last week too, didn't you?

A: Goodbye. Please come again.
B: Thank you. I'll drop by again.

A: Well, see you.
B: See you.
fields.explain: Expresses that the same thing happens repeatedly. As in 4. ～6., it is also used as a greeting when parting.

fields.meaning: Want (someone) to … (so that …)

Expresses the highest degree (comparison)
limitation, ultimate limit
examples: For now, there is no textbook easier to understand than this one.
It's rare to find a movie more worthless than that one.
Even if you searched all over Japan, you probably wouldn't find anyone smarter than that person.
fields.explain: Attaches mainly to 「これ／それ／あれ」 and expresses that what they point to has the highest degree. 「一番…だ」.

fields.meaning:
Expresses continuation
unchanging state
examples: Japanese tomatoes taste better eaten raw, without cooking them.
Clerk: Shall I put it in a bag for you? Customer: No, it's fine as it is.
Even as I get older, I want to stay beautiful.
Many people drink sake warmed, but I like to drink it cold, as it is.
Please do not enter the room with your shoes on.
If you sleep with the air conditioner on, you'll catch a cold.
fields.explain:
Expresses the meaning 「変化せずに同じ状態で」. As in 1. ～4., it expresses not changing the current state or something not changing, and as in 5. ～⑩, it attaches to the た-form or negative form of a verb and expresses the meaning 「その状態で…する」. It is used with verbs expressing instantaneous actions, when the next action or event takes place while the result of that action continues. The subjects of the two verbs must be the same.
*（誤） 電車はこんでいて、山田さんは立ったまま、私はすわっていた。
*（正） 電車はこんでいて、山田さんは立ったままだったが、私はすわっていた。
*（誤） 彼が待っているまま、私は他の人と話していた。
*（正） 彼を待たせたまま、私は他の人と話していた。
fields.notes: In spoken language, 「まんま」 is also used.

fields.meaning: Expresses limitation, ultimate limit
examples: I took the exam three times and finally passed.
The test is finally over, too.
After practicing for days, I was finally able to do it.
I have finally recovered to the point where I can leave the hospital.
The tunnel was finally completed in 1995.
I scolded my grandchild sternly, and they finally stopped playing pranks.
fields.explain:
Expresses that something the speaker had been longing for comes about after hardship or after a very long time. It is often used in the form 「やっとＶ－た」. It expresses the speaker's "relief" or "joy," or feelings such as "it took a long time" or "it was hard." Similar expressions are 「ようやく」「とうとう」「ついに」. 「とうとう」 and 「ついに」 can be used both for things that are desirable for the speaker and for things that are not, but 「やっと」 can only be used for things the speaker had been longing for.
*（例） 長い間入院していた祖父が｛とうとう／ついに｝亡くなった。
!If 「やっと」 is used in an example like the one above, it would mean the speaker "had long been waiting for grandfather to die." 「とうとう／ついに」 are neutral expressions that indicate that, after a long time or process, the final stage was reached, regardless of whether the speaker wanted it. Also, since 「やっと」「ようやく」 are used when something the speaker had been longing for comes about, they cannot express that something did not happen in the end.
*（誤） 彼は、｛やっと／ようやく｝来なかった。
*（正） 彼は、｛とうとう／ついに｝来なかった。

fields.name: （particle）なら
examples: If it's with that person, I wouldn't mind getting married.
I'm no good at French, but in English I can hold a conversation.
If it's just one more person, they can still get in.
If it's after work, I have time.

A: How is your leg?
B: I can walk now, as long as it's slowly.
fields.explain:
Takes a noun, an adverb, or a noun + particle, etc., and expresses the meaning 「他の場合はそうでないが、Ｘについてなら／の場合ならＹが成立する」. Y is usually followed by something desirable, and it is used when actively choosing an X that makes it possible. It is similar to 「は」 expressing contrast, but 「なら」 can take question words, whereas 「は」 cannot.
*（正） 何時なら都合がいいですか。誰となら結婚してもいいですか。
*（誤） 何時は都合がいいですか。誰とは結婚してもいいですか。

fields.meaning: Expresses a future action that has been arranged, or a future action decided by a third party.
examples: It has been decided that we will go to the venue by bus.
I will probably be the one to make the restaurant reservation.
I'm going to the United States on a business trip next month.
It has been decided that the next class reunion will be held in Tokyo.
I'm happy that I'm going to receive a scholarship.
Another group is using the meeting room, so it turns out we can't use it.
fields.explain: ◎ Something is decided to be done that way according to some situation or condition.
fields.notes:
Note:
●自分の意志で決めた場合でも、ほかの人に報告するときは「～ことになる」を使うことが多い。
Even when it is your own decision, 「～ことになる」 is often used when reporting it to others.
「わたしたち、来月結婚することになりました」
「We have decided that we will get married.」
meaning_vi: Expresses things such as habits, rules, or plans that you did not decide yourself.
読む／読まない　+　ことになった／ことになっている
explain: ◎ Expresses that some action or state leads to some result.
examples: 1. 落ち着いてください。あわてると、ミスをすることになります。
Please calm down. Rushing will lead to mistakes.
2. 今、部長に報告しておかないと、あとで面倒なことになる。
If you don't report to the department manager now, it will lead to trouble later.
──────
1. ①　待つことになった
I had to wait
2. ②　来月から東京本社で働くことになった。
I will work at the head office in Tokyo starting next month.
3. ③　私の会社では、新入社員は朝、掃除することになっている。
At my company, new employees clean every morning.
4. ➃　１０時からA社の田中さんと会うことになっている。
I am scheduled to meet Mr. Tanaka of Company A at 10 o'clock.

fields.meaning: About, concerning
examples: Let me explain the new system.
The police are investigating the cause of the incident.
I bought an introductory book about history.
This matter is currently under consideration within the company.
We are asking for opinions on changing the terms of use.
I have a question about product safety.
fields.explain:
Used with 動詞/名詞 such as 説明・議論・報告・質問・情報・意見・調査.
“については” separates out a topic for emphasis/contrast; “についても” adds to the scope.
In official documents, titles often use “Nについての研究/報告/方針”.

• Establishes the topic of discussion, research, or explanation: “about/concerning N”.
• Suitable for both spoken and written language; neutral and easy to use.
• The scope is usually more specific than に関して (which is more general and formal).
fields.notes:
• When the topic is already clear, it can be replaced with それ/この件 to avoid repetition.
• Do not use “について” to cite a source of information (use “によると/によれば”).
• In emails, “件名：Nについて” is a natural way to write a subject line.
meaning_vi: 「～の内容・～に関係があることを…する。」～は話題を表す言葉。…は「思う・考える・話す・聞く・調べる・書く・説明する・知っている」などの動詞の文。
Do … about the content of ~ / something related to ~.
~ is a word expressing the topic.
… is a sentence with verbs such as 思う／考える／話す／きく／調べる／書く／説明する／知っている…
examples: 1. すみません、入学手続きについて聞きたいのですが…。
Excuse me, I'd like to ask about the enrollment procedures...
2. 今、私の国の教育についてレポートを書いています。
I'm currently writing a report on education in my country.
3. この作品についての感想を話していただけません。
Could you tell me your impressions of this work? | Formal variant: ～につき
mistakes: Forgetting “の” when modifying a noun: it must be “NについてのN2”.
Confusing “に対して” (direction of an action) with “について” (topic).
Using “について” for a source of information is the wrong function; use “によれば/によると”.
Machine translation easily mistakes “about” for “で”: the correct form is “について”.

rows: <ruby>計画<rt>けいかく</rt></ruby>について<ruby>話<rt>はな</rt></ruby>す。
<ruby>法律<rt>ほうりつ</rt></ruby>に<ruby>関<rt>かん</rt></ruby>して<ruby>発表<rt>はっぴょう</rt></ruby>する。
<ruby>予算<rt>よさん</rt></ruby>をめぐって<ruby>議論<rt>ぎろん</rt></ruby>する。
<ruby>子<rt>こ</rt></ruby>どもに<ruby>対<rt>たい</rt></ruby>して<ruby>優<rt>やさ</rt></ruby>しい。

fields.meaning: ~ do nothing but
examples: If you do nothing but play, you won't be able to graduate.
Even during the meal, she did nothing but look at her phone.
fields.explain: ◎ Always doing that thing; used in the form「～て ばかりいる」.
fields.notes:
meaning_vi: 「ほかのことはしないで、よく～する。」非難の気持ちで言う。
Not doing other things, but often doing ~.
Often used with a nuance of criticism.
examples: 1. 祖父は最近怒ってばかりいる
祖父は最近怒ってばかりいる=> My grandfather is always getting angry these days.
2. 二十歳のころは遊んでばかりいた。勉強しなかったことを今は残念に思っている。
二十歳のころは遊んでばかりいた。勉強しなかったことを今は残念に思っている。=> When I was twenty, I did nothing but play. Now I regret not having studied.
3. ただ見てばかりいないで、少しは手伝ってくださいよ。
ただ見てばかりいないで、少しは手伝ってくださいよ。=> Don't just stand there watching; help out a little.
meaning_vi: ～ばかり Expresses a large degree and only one thing. ～てばかりいる Refers to an action that happens frequently. This sentence pattern is often used to express criticism.
examples: 1. ①　ゲームばかりして
Doing nothing but playing games
2. ②　10円玉ばかり　あっても、うれしくない。
Even if I have lots of coins, if they're all 10-yen coins, I'm not happy.
3. ③　チョコレートばかり　食べていると、太りますよ。
If you eat nothing but chocolate, you'll gain weight.
4. ③　あそんでばかりいると、試験に　合格できないよ。
If you do nothing but play, you won't pass the exam.
5. ④　泣いてばかりいても　だめだよ。しっかり　説明して。
Just crying won't help. Explain it properly.
meaning_vi: Continuing the same state or action without change. Carries a meaning of criticism.
examples: 1. ①　寝てばかりだ
Doing nothing but sleeping
2. ②　弟は毎日寝てばかりだ。
My younger brother does nothing but sleep every day.
3. ➂　遊んでばかりいないで、勉強しなさい。
Stop doing nothing but playing, and study.

fields.name: ～V causative form ていただけませんか
fields.meaning: Would you please allow me to ~
fields.connection: V causative form て + いただけませんか
examples:
A: Excuse me, sir. A friend of mine is getting married next week. Would you allow me to take two days off?
B: I see. That's fine.

A: Excuse me. Would you mind if I parked my car here for a little while? I need to unload some luggage.
B: Sure.
fields.explain:
◎ Combines the causative expression with "～てくれる" to express gratitude.

Politely asks for permission to do something.
The sentence patterns in the box are arranged in order of increasing politeness.
fields.notes:
examples: 1. 「熱があるかもしれません」と言うと、店長は早めに帰らせてくれた。
When I said, "I might have a fever," the store manager let me go home early.
2. 留学させてくれたことを親に感謝しています。
I am truly grateful to my parents for letting me study abroad.
meaning_vi: 「（自分が）～する/～しないことを望む。」 ほかの人が自分のために、ある状況を作ったり許可したりすることを望む言い方。 ②③のように、相手に直接希望を言うときにもよく使う。
(You yourself) want to be allowed to do ~ / not do ~.
An expression of the desire for someone else to create conditions for you or give you permission to do something.
As in examples ②③, this structure is often used to state your wish directly to the other person.
examples: 1. 店員A「昼休みが短いよね。昼ご飯をもっとゆっくり食べさせてもらいたいね。」
店員B「そうだね。店長に行ってみよう。」
meaning_vi: Asking for permission to perform one's own action.
examples: 1. ①　使わせてもらえますか
May I use it?
2. ②　すみません、この電話、使わせてもらえますか。
Excuse me, may I use this phone?
3. ➂　私も会議に出させてもらえませんか。
Could you let me attend the meeting too?
4. ➃　うちの商品をお店に置かせていただけませんでしょうか。
Would you allow us to sell our products in your store?
